newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: South Asian delegates to monitor Pakistan polls.
newsitem.headline: South Asian delegates to monitor Pakistan polls.

text.p: A 41-member delegation from four South Asian countries will monitor Monday's elections in Pakistan, a member of the group said on Saturday.
"The purpose of our visit is more to learn and understand about the Pakistani elections," said Feroze Hasan, a delegate from Bangladesh.

The non-governmental delegation, coordinated by the Sri Lankan Institute of Ethnic Studies, has members from India, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka and Nepal. The Human Rights Commission of Pakistan is providing assistance.
Hasan, who is the Secretary-General of the Fair Election Monitoring Alliance, Bangladesh, said the delegates would go to rural and urban areas in all of Pakistan's four provinces.
"It is too early to give an opinion, but Pakistani elections are very dull compared to Bangladesh. In fact, there is nothing like elections -- no posters, no public enthusiasm," he said.
"People are rallying around only big leaders who are running their campaign through chartered helicopters and aeroplanes."
He said the delegation members would meet on Tuesday to compile a report about the conduct of the elections.
The polls were called by President Farooq Leghari after he dismissed Benazir Bhutto government's on November 5 and dissolved the 217-seat National Assembly (lower house).
The Supreme Court on Wednesday upheld Leghari's action, saying there was evidence of corruption, nepotism and misrule.
Bhutto, who denies the charges, accuses Leghari of seeking to rig election results in some constituencies against her Pakistan People's Party.
